result: Human telomerase unfolds both intramolecular and intermolecular parallel G-quadruplexes through a three-step mechanism: (1) binding and partial unfolding involving the RNA template, (2) nucleotide addition to the partially unfolded G4, and (3) complete unfolding via translocation.
evaluation: Claims C40-C43 and C55, C125 are supported by comprehensive smFRET data showing two-step FRET drops (Figures 2, 4), experiments with catalytically inactive telomerase (Figure 5), RNA oligonucleotide experiments (Figure 5F-J), and subset dNTP experiments (Figure 6). The mechanistic model is consistently demonstrated across both G4 topologies with quantitative kinetic analysis.

result: 2'F-araG modification of telomeric sequences creates stable parallel intramolecular G4 that are efficiently extended by telomerase with the expected 6-nt repeat pattern.
evaluation: Claims C54, C56, C80 are supported by direct telomerase extension assays (Figure 1B, Figure 3B) showing restoration of proper extension patterns. The CD spectroscopy and thermal stability data (Figure 1D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1) confirm parallel topology and increased stability.

result: Both F-22G3 and F-[7GGT]4 G-quadruplexes exhibit stable FRET signals (~0.5 and ~0.6 respectively) over time in the absence of telomerase, confirming formation of stable parallel G4 structures.
evaluation: Claims C58-C59, C64-C65, C81-C83 are supported by smFRET data showing constant FRET ratios over 150s (Figures 2A-B, 4A-B) and Li+ control experiments showing FRET drops upon G4 destabilization (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).

result: Telomerase binding alone (without dNTPs) causes partial G4 unfolding, evidenced by a single FRET drop from ~0.5-0.6 to ~0.3-0.4 in approximately 60-65% of molecules.
evaluation: Claims C66, C68, C85, C87 are supported by smFRET experiments showing single FRET drops in the presence of telomerase without dNTPs (Figures 2D-F, 4D-F). TDP analysis confirms unidirectional transitions (Figure 2F, 4F).

result: In the presence of both telomerase and dNTPs, approximately 65% of G4 molecules undergo a two-step irreversible FRET decrease, indicating complete G4 disruption.
evaluation: Claims C70, C72, C88, C90 are supported by smFRET data showing two-step FRET drops (Figures 2G-I, 4G-I) and TDP analysis showing two off-diagonal clusters indicating irreversible transitions. Control experiments with dNTPs alone show no FRET changes (Figure 2—figure supplement 3, Figure 4—figure supplement 3).

result: The unfolding rates of F-22G3 (0.120 ± 0.013 s⁻¹) and F-[7GGT]4 (0.073 ± 0.013 s⁻¹) by telomerase are comparable to each other and to Pif1 helicase, with gamma distribution analysis indicating 2-3 rate-limiting steps.
evaluation: Claims C73-C76, C94-C96 are supported by dwell time analysis fitted to gamma distributions (Figure 2—figure supplement 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 4A). The rates are quantified with appropriate statistical measures (mean ± SEM) and compared to published helicase rates.

result: At low dGTP concentration, G4 unfolding reveals additional kinetic complexity with at least 5 independent steps whose rates are influenced by dNTP concentration.
evaluation: Claims C97-C101 are supported by smFRET experiments at 100-fold lower dGTP showing gradual transitions (Figure 4—figure supplement 4B-D). Gamma distribution analysis reveals multiple rate-limiting steps (2-3 for first transition, 3-4 for second), supporting the conclusion of at least 5 total steps.

result: Catalytically inactive D712A telomerase causes partial but not complete G4 unfolding, demonstrating that full unwinding requires telomerase catalytic activity.
evaluation: Claims C104-C106, C117 are supported by smFRET experiments with D712A mutant showing only single FRET drop even with dNTPs (Figure 5A-E) and activity assays confirming loss of extension activity (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).

result: A 10-nt RNA oligonucleotide mimicking the telomerase template (RNA.10C) induces G4 unfolding similar to the whole enzyme, while a DNA oligonucleotide of identical sequence does not, demonstrating RNA-specific G4 interaction.
evaluation: Claims C110-C111, C115-C116, C166 are supported by smFRET experiments showing FRET drops with RNA.10C but not DNA.10C (Figure 5F-J). The concentration-dependent effect and dynamic behavior (Figure 5—figure supplement 2) support the interpretation of specific RNA-G4 interaction.

result: Complete G4 unfolding occurs only after addition of three nucleotides (reaching the template boundary), as demonstrated by subset dNTP experiments showing the second FRET drop only with dTTP, dATP, and ddGTP.
evaluation: Claims C118-C124 are supported by systematic smFRET experiments with different dNTP combinations (Figure 6, Figure 6—figure supplement 2-3). The data clearly show single FRET drops with incomplete nucleotide sets and two-step drops only when the template boundary can be reached.

result: Ligand stabilization of intramolecular parallel G4 (F-22G3) partially inhibits telomerase activity, reducing the fraction of molecules showing two-step FRET drops by ~2-fold, but 25-30% of molecules are still unfolded and extended.
evaluation: Claims C131-C134, C142-C143 are supported by smFRET data showing reduced but not eliminated G4 unfolding in the presence of NMM, SST16, and PhenDC3 (Figure 7A-J). Ensemble activity assays confirm partial inhibition (Figure 7—figure supplement 5).

result: NMM significantly slows the unfolding rate of F-22G3 (0.071 ± 0.014 s⁻¹ vs 0.12 ± 0.013 s⁻¹, p=0.0118), providing evidence that ligand-bound molecules are unfolded more slowly by telomerase.
evaluation: Claims C135-C138 are supported by quantitative dwell time analysis with statistical testing (Figure 7K, Figure 7—figure supplement 4). The significant p-value and reduced rate provide strong evidence for ligand-mediated slowing of unfolding.

result: Ligand stabilization of intermolecular parallel G4 ([7GGT]4) does not inhibit telomerase extension, with NMM and SST16 showing no inhibition at any concentration tested.
evaluation: Claims C146, C151-C152 are supported by ensemble telomerase activity assays showing no reduction in extension with NMM or SST16 (Figure 8A-D, Figure 8—figure supplement 2A-B). The dramatic thermal stabilization (ΔTm +13-21°C) confirms ligand binding.

result: Ligand-stabilized F-[7GGT]4 still undergoes telomerase-mediated conformational changes and complete unfolding, with most molecules showing the characteristic two-step FRET decrease.
evaluation: Claims C154-C156, C159 are supported by smFRET data showing single FRET drops with telomerase alone and two-step drops with telomerase and dNTPs in the presence of all three ligands (Figure 9A-J).

result: SST16 significantly accelerates F-[7GGT]4 unfolding (0.28 ± 0.07 s⁻¹ vs 0.073 ± 0.013 s⁻¹, p=0.021), while NMM and PhenDC3 do not significantly change the unfolding rate.
evaluation: Claims C157-C158 are supported by quantitative dwell time analysis with statistical testing (Figure 9K, Figure 9—figure supplement 3). The significant acceleration with SST16 is unexpected but well-documented with appropriate statistics.

result: Small molecule-mediated inhibition of telomerase extension of telomeric G4 is topology-dependent, with ligands partially inhibiting intramolecular but not intermolecular parallel G4 extension.
evaluation: Claim C45 is supported by the contrasting effects of ligands on F-22G3 (partial inhibition) versus [7GGT]4 (no inhibition) demonstrated through both smFRET and ensemble activity assays (Figures 7-9). This represents a key conclusion integrating multiple experimental observations.

result: Molecular modeling supports a mechanism where hTERT conformational changes during translocation open the active site, allowing G4 strand separation, with simulations showing 5' ends moving apart after 100 ns.
evaluation: Claims C160-C162 are based on molecular dynamics simulations (Figure 10) which provide plausible structural models but lack experimental validation. The authors appropriately note this is 'in silico simulation rather than direct structural observation.' The model is consistent with experimental data but requires structural confirmation.

result: Telomerase itself has the ability to unwind parallel G4 without assistance from interacting helicases, as demonstrated using highly purified enzyme.
evaluation: Claim C163 is supported by prior work (Moye et al., 2015) showing highly purified telomerase extends [7GGT]4. The current smFRET data with purified enzyme further supports this conclusion by demonstrating the complete unfolding mechanism.

result: Telomerase functions as a parallel G-quadruplex resolvase, directly interacting with and resolving parallel G4 structures without forming a barrier to extension.
evaluation: Claims C8, C185, C187 represent the central conclusion of the manuscript, supported by the comprehensive demonstration of G4 binding, unfolding, and extension across multiple experimental approaches (smFRET, ensemble assays, kinetic analysis). The data unequivocally demonstrate telomerase's resolvase activity.

result: All three G4 ligands (NMM, SST16, PhenDC3) dramatically stabilize both intramolecular and intermolecular parallel G4 structures (ΔTm +11 to >25°C) without changing their parallel topology.
evaluation: Claims C128-C129, C144-C145 are supported by CD spectroscopy showing maintained parallel topology and thermal denaturation assays showing substantial ΔTm increases (Figure 7—figure supplement 2, Figure 8—figure supplement 1).

result: PhenDC3 decreases telomerase processivity after 4 repeats on both linear and G4 substrates, likely through stabilization of G4 in product DNA, and shows G4-independent inhibition at concentrations >1 µM.
evaluation: Claims C147-C150 are supported by ensemble activity assays (Figure 8C, Figure 8—figure supplement 2C) and consistent with prior literature (De Cian et al., 2007a). The effect on both substrates clearly indicates G4-independent mechanisms at higher concentrations.

result: Substitution of six guanosines with 2'F-araG in AGGG(TTAGGG)3 increases Tm by 15°C and shifts the topology from antiparallel/hybrid to parallel conformation.
evaluation: Claims C51-C52 are supported by citations to prior work from the authors (Abou Assi et al., 2017) and confirmed by CD spectroscopy in the current study (Figure 1D). This is established methodology enabling the key experiments.

result: Unmodified 22G0 in KCl is a poor telomerase substrate, producing a stuttering extension pattern rather than the expected 6-nt repeats.
evaluation: Claim C53 is supported by direct extension assays (Figure 1B, lane 3) and consistent with prior literature (Zaug et al., 2005). This validates the need for the 2'F-araG modification to study intramolecular parallel G4.

result: The tetrameric parallel G4 [7GGT]4 is highly stable, unambiguously parallel in topology (too short for intramolecular folding), and can be extended by human telomerase.
evaluation: Claims C77-C79 are supported by prior work (Gavathiotis and Searle, 2003; Moye et al., 2015) and confirmed by CD spectroscopy and extension assays in the current study (Figure 3). This provides the intermolecular parallel G4 model system.

result: Mutation of conserved aspartate residues in the TERT reverse transcriptase domain (e.g., D712A) eliminates catalytic activity while retaining DNA binding ability.
evaluation: Claims C102-C103 are supported by prior literature and confirmed by activity assays showing complete loss of extension (Figure 5—figure supplement 1). This validates the use of D712A to separate binding from catalytic functions.

result: Template-mimicking RNA cannot form DNA-RNA hybrids with antiparallel G4 of similar stability, demonstrating specificity of the RNA-parallel G4 interaction.
evaluation: Claims C167-C168 are supported by citation to prior work (Birrento et al., 2015) and consistent with the current DNA.10C control experiments. This supports the specificity of the mechanism for parallel G4.

result: Conformational changes during translocation result in complete G4 unfolding, with ddGTP incorporation compatible with subsequent DNA realignment and template rehybridization.
evaluation: Claims C170-C171 are supported by prior smFRET work (Parks and Stone, 2014) showing ddGTP compatibility with translocation, and the current observation of second FRET drops after reaching the template boundary. The inference is well-supported.

result: Telomerase can dislodge ligands from tetramolecular G4 structures while unfolding them, similar to RHAU helicase.
evaluation: Claim C173 is supported by the demonstration that ligand-stabilized [7GGT]4 is still unfolded and extended (Figures 8-9). The comparison to RHAU helicase (Gueddouda et al., 2017; Tippana et al., 2016) provides mechanistic context.

result: The conserved ability of human and ciliate telomerase to unwind parallel G4 suggests these structures form at telomeric overhangs in vivo.
evaluation: Claim C186 is an inference based on evolutionary conservation. While the conservation is documented (C31-C32), the in vivo formation of parallel G4 at telomeres remains uncertain (C177-C178). The suggestion is reasonable but requires direct in vivo evidence.
